description: LLVM IR vocabulary as graph data. Each lesson is a `learn_from_teacher`-shaped payload; the loader replays them into the agent at boot so the standard Frame layer answers LLVM-concept questions without a teacher round-trip.

payload.answer: LLVM Intermediate Representation: a typed, SSA-form, RISC-like virtual instruction set used as the common language for LLVM's analyses, transformations, and code generators.
The top-level container in LLVM IR. Holds global variables, function declarations and definitions, type definitions, target triple, and metadata.
A named code unit in an LLVM Module with a return type, parameter list, calling convention, and a body of basic blocks. May be declared (external) or defined (with body).
A maximal straight-line sequence of LLVM instructions ending in exactly one terminator. Has a label and is the unit of control-flow target. The entry block of a function has no predecessors.
A single operation in LLVM IR. Has an opcode, operands (Values), and possibly a result Value with a Type. Instructions are organised into Basic Blocks.
Any first-class entity in LLVM IR that produces a result: a constant, a function argument, the output of an instruction, a global variable, or a basic block (when used as a branch target).

The classification of an LLVM Value's data. Every Value has a Type known at compile time. Categories: integer (iN), floating-point, pointer, vector, array, struct, function, void, label, metadata, token.

Static Single Assignment: a code form where every variable is assigned exactly once and defined before use. Makes def-use chains explicit; LLVM IR is in SSA form. Multiple control-flow paths producing a value join via phi instructions.
The last instruction of a basic block. Determines where control flow goes next: ret, br, switch, indirectbr, invoke, callbr, resume, catchswitch, catchret, cleanupret, or unreachable.
A scalar integer of an arbitrary bit width N, written iN (e.g. i1 boolean, i8 byte, i32, i64). Bit width is part of the type; the interpretation as signed or unsigned depends on the operation.
IEEE-754 floating-point types: half (16-bit), bfloat, float (32-bit), double (64-bit), fp128 (128-bit), x86_fp80, ppc_fp128. Distinct from integer types.
An address in some address space, written ptr (opaque, since LLVM 15) or T* (typed, deprecated). Pointers carry an address space (default 0).
The type of a function value: return type, parameter types, and a varargs flag. Written like <ret>(<params>) — e.g. i32(i32, ptr).
The empty return type — used for functions that produce no value. Cannot appear as a value's type (no SSA register holds it).
LLVM integer addition. add iN X, Y returns X + Y. Optional flags nsw/nuw mark signed/unsigned overflow as undefined behaviour (poison value).
LLVM integer subtraction. sub iN X, Y returns X - Y. Optional nsw/nuw mark signed/unsigned overflow as undefined behaviour (poison value).
LLVM integer multiplication. mul iN X, Y returns X * Y (modulo 2^N). Optional nsw/nuw flags mark signed/unsigned overflow as undefined.
LLVM unsigned integer division. udiv iN X, Y returns X / Y treating both as unsigned. Division by zero is undefined behaviour. exact flag marks remainder-of-zero division for the optimiser.
LLVM signed integer division. sdiv iN X, Y returns X / Y truncating toward zero, treating both as two's-complement signed. Division by zero and INT_MIN/-1 are undefined.
LLVM unsigned integer remainder. urem iN X, Y returns X mod Y treating both as unsigned. Division by zero is undefined.
LLVM signed integer remainder. srem iN X, Y returns X mod Y where (X/Y)*Y + (X%Y) = X using truncated division. Sign of result follows X.
LLVM floating-point negation. fneg F X returns -X. Optional fast-math flags (nnan/ninf/nsz/arcp/...) permit relaxed IEEE-754 semantics.
LLVM floating-point addition. fadd F X, Y returns X + Y per IEEE-754. Optional fast-math flags permit reassociation, NaN/inf assumptions, reciprocal approximations.
LLVM floating-point subtraction. fsub F X, Y returns X - Y per IEEE-754. Fast-math flags apply.
LLVM floating-point multiplication. fmul F X, Y returns X * Y per IEEE-754. Fast-math flags apply.
LLVM floating-point division. fdiv F X, Y returns X / Y per IEEE-754. Fast-math flag arcp permits X * (1/Y) substitution.
LLVM floating-point remainder. frem F X, Y returns the remainder of X / Y. Semantics match libm's fmod (not IEEE-754 remainder).
Read a value of a given Type from a memory address. load T, ptr P returns the value of type T at address P. May carry alignment, volatile, and atomicity annotations.
Write a Value to a memory address. store V, ptr P writes V at address P. May carry alignment, volatile, and atomicity annotations. No result.
Integer compare. icmp <pred> iN X, Y returns i1. Predicates: eq, ne, ugt, uge, ult, ule, sgt, sge, slt, sle (signed/unsigned variants for ordering).
Branch — the simplest control-flow terminator. Conditional: br i1 cond, label %then, label %else. Unconditional: br label %target. Targets must be basic blocks within the same function.
The SSA merge instruction. phi T [v1, %bb1], [v2, %bb2], ... selects the value corresponding to the predecessor block control entered from. Must appear at the start of its basic block.
Stack-allocate space for a value. alloca T returns a pointer (in alloca address space, default 0) to freshly-allocated stack memory of size sizeof(T). Lifetime ends at function return.

Compute an address from a base pointer and a sequence of indices, navigating the pointee's type structure. Pure address arithmetic — does not read memory. Abbreviated GEP. The most common cause of confusion in LLVM IR.
Function return — a terminator. ret T V returns value V of type T; ret void returns from a void function. The function's return type must match.
LLVM bitwise AND. and iN X, Y returns the bitwise conjunction of X and Y. Operates on integer types and vectors of integers.
LLVM bitwise OR. or iN X, Y returns the bitwise disjunction of X and Y.
LLVM bitwise XOR. xor iN X, Y returns the bitwise exclusive-or of X and Y. xor X, -1 inverts (logical NOT).
LLVM logical shift left. shl iN X, Y returns X shifted left by Y bits. Optional nsw/nuw mark signed/unsigned overflow as undefined.
LLVM logical shift right. lshr iN X, Y returns X shifted right by Y bits, filling with zeros. Unsigned semantics.
LLVM arithmetic shift right. ashr iN X, Y returns X shifted right by Y bits, sign-extending. Preserves the sign of two's-complement integers.

Atomic read-modify-write. atomicrmw <op> ptr P, V atomically performs a binop on *P with V and returns the OLD value at P. Ops: xchg, add, sub, and, nand, or, xor, max, min, umax, umin, fadd, fsub, fmax, fmin. Requires an ordering.

Atomic compare-and-swap. cmpxchg ptr P, V_cmp, V_new atomically: if *P == V_cmp store V_new. Returns { value_at_P, success_bool }. Requires success and failure memory orderings. Foundation of lock-free algorithms.

Memory ordering barrier. fence <ordering> enforces the given memory ordering between atomic operations in this thread (and across threads for sequentially consistent fences). No data motion; pure ordering constraint.
The synchronisation guarantee on an atomic op. Kinds (weakest to strongest): unordered, monotonic, acquire, release, acq_rel, seq_cst. Determines what other ops can be reordered around this one.
Truncate an integer to a smaller integer type. trunc iN X to iM drops the high bits. M < N.
Zero-extend an integer to a larger integer type. zext iN X to iM pads high bits with zeros. M > N.
Sign-extend an integer to a larger integer type. sext iN X to iM pads high bits with the sign bit. M > N.
Reinterpret a value's bits as a different type without changing the bits. bitcast T1 X to T2. T1 and T2 must have the same size. Used heavily for pointer-type punning before opaque pointers.
Convert a pointer to an integer. ptrtoint ptr X to iN. The integer is the address; size depends on the data layout.
Convert an integer to a pointer. inttoptr iN X to ptr. Treats the integer as an address.
Convert a signed integer to a floating-point value. sitofp iN X to F. Rounds per the target FP environment.
Convert an unsigned integer to a floating-point value. uitofp iN X to F. Rounds per the target FP environment.
Convert a floating-point value to a signed integer. fptosi F X to iN. Truncates toward zero. Out-of-range values produce poison.
Convert a floating-point value to an unsigned integer. fptoui F X to iN. Truncates toward zero. Out-of-range values produce poison.
Convert a floating-point value to a smaller FP type. fptrunc F1 X to F2 with F1 wider than F2. Rounds per the target FP environment.
Extend a floating-point value to a wider FP type. fpext F1 X to F2 with F2 wider than F1. Exact — wider types representable supersets of narrower.
Cast a pointer between address spaces. addrspacecast ptr addrspace(N) X to ptr addrspace(M). Semantics target-defined; on most targets the address bit pattern may differ.

Stop poison/undef propagation. freeze T X returns an arbitrary fixed concrete value when X is poison or undef, X otherwise. Useful when a use needs a well-defined value but the producer might be undefined.

Floating-point compare. fcmp <pred> F X, Y returns i1. Predicates: oeq, ogt, oge, olt, ole, one, ord (ordered: neither is NaN); ueq, ugt, uge, ult, ule, une, uno (unordered: either is NaN). Plus true/false.
Three-way value select. select i1 cond, T A, T B returns A if cond is true, else B. Branchless conditional value.
Call a function. call ret_type @fn(args) invokes the named function with the given arguments and returns its result. May carry calling convention, fast-math flags, and function attributes.

Call a function with exception-aware control flow. invoke ret_type @fn(args) to label %normal unwind label %unwind. Returns normally to %normal; an uncaught exception jumps to %unwind. Acts as a terminator.
Multi-way branch — a terminator. switch iN val, label %default [iN c1, label %b1 ; iN c2, label %b2 ; ...]. Dispatches on val against each case; falls to %default on no match.
A terminator indicating control flow cannot reach this point. The optimizer may treat reaching it as undefined behaviour. Common after explicit exhaustive dispatch.
Read a field from an aggregate value (struct or array). extractvalue T agg, idx0, idx1, ... walks the type structure. Result is the typed field.
Produce a new aggregate value with one field replaced. insertvalue T agg, ET v, idx0, idx1, ... returns a new aggregate of type T identical to agg except at the indexed field.
Read one lane from a vector. extractelement <N x T> V, iM idx returns the element at index idx. Out-of-range index is undefined.
Produce a new vector with one lane replaced. insertelement <N x T> V, T elt, iM idx returns a new vector identical to V except at lane idx, which holds elt. Out-of-range index is undefined.
Permute lanes across two vectors. shufflevector <N x T> A, <N x T> B, <M x i32> mask returns an M-element vector whose i-th lane is A[mask[i]] if mask[i] < N, B[mask[i]-N] if < 2N, undef if -1.

Indirect branch — a terminator. indirectbr ptr addr, [label %b1, label %b2, ...] jumps to the block whose address equals addr. addr must be a blockaddress of one of the listed blocks. Used for computed goto.
Call that can branch to multiple targets — a terminator. callbr ret @fn(args) to label %normal [label %other1, label %other2, ...]. Used for inline asm with multiple outputs / labels.
Resume propagation of a caught exception — a terminator. resume T excval transfers control to the caller's exception handler, continuing the unwind started by an invoke.

The first instruction of an invoke's unwind block. landingpad T <clauses> describes the personality function's catch/filter clauses and produces the exception value(s). Required at the entry of an unwind handler.

Begin a catch handler in Windows SEH-style exception handling. catchpad within %parent [<args>] sets up a token used by catchret to transfer control. Counterpart to landingpad for the funclet personality.
Begin a cleanup handler in Windows SEH-style exception handling. cleanuppad within %parent [<args>] sets up a token used by cleanupret to transfer control after finally-style cleanup runs.
Terminator that exits a catch handler back to normal control flow. catchret from %catchpad to label %target. Counterpart to catchpad.
Terminator that exits a cleanup handler. cleanupret from %cleanuppad unwind [to caller | label %target]. Resumes unwinding after finally-style cleanup runs.
A heterogeneous, fixed-layout aggregate. { T1, T2, ... } enumerates field types in order. May be literal or named (identified by name). Fields are accessed by getelementptr / extractvalue.
A homogeneous, fixed-length sequence of one type. [N x T] is an array of N elements of type T. Accessed by getelementptr / extractvalue.
A SIMD-style fixed-length sequence of a scalar type. <N x T> for N elements of T. Operations on vectors apply element-wise. Used for vectorisation and SIMD codegen.
An LLVM Value whose contents are fixed at compile time. Includes literal integers / floats / strings, named constants, undef, poison, null, and constant expressions built from other constants.
The null pointer constant — `null` (or `@G = ... = ptr null`). Has type ptr (pointer in address space 0); addrspacecast'able to other spaces. Dereferencing is undefined.
An unspecified value of any type — the compiler may choose any bit pattern at its discretion (and may choose different ones at different uses). Distinct from poison (less constrained than undef).
A constant of any type whose bytes are all zero. Convenience for aggregate / vector / pointer zero values. Written `zeroinitializer`.
A module-scope Value allocated for the lifetime of the program. Has linkage, an optional initialiser, address space, alignment, and attributes. Accessed by name (@G).

The ABI rule for passing arguments, receiving results, and saving/restoring registers across a call. LLVM-named conventions: ccc (C, default), fastcc, coldcc, tailcc, anyregcc, and many target-specific variants.

How a symbol's name resolves across translation units. Common kinds: external (visible across TUs), internal (TU-local), private (named-but-local), weak (overridable), common (uninitialized weak), available_externally.
A flag or value attached to a function or call that informs analyses and codegen. Examples: noinline, alwaysinline, readnone, readonly, norecurse, nounwind, nofree, willreturn, cold, hot, optsize.

A numbered address namespace for pointers. Space 0 is the default (target's normal flat space); other spaces have target-specific semantics (e.g. shared, constant, private on GPUs). Pointer types carry their address space.
Non-semantic annotations attached to instructions, modules, and globals. Carries debug info, optimization hints, type info, range constraints. Written !name. Stripped does not change behaviour.
The graph linking each Value's definition (the instruction that produced it) to every Use (the operand slot referencing it). LLVM IR makes def-use chains explicit and traversable in O(1) per step.
A result that came from an operation with undefined behaviour (e.g. signed overflow under nsw). Propagates: any operation consuming poison produces poison. Distinct from undef (less constrained).
In a control-flow graph, a block A dominates B iff every path from entry to B passes through A. The dominator relation underpins SSA construction, Mem2Reg, LICM, and most code-motion passes.

A traversal of LLVM IR that analyses or transforms it. Categories: analysis passes (compute information), transformation passes (rewrite IR), and utility passes. Composed into pipelines; ordering matters.
